newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada no-frills flier grounded in maintenance row.
newsitem.headline: Canada no-frills flier grounded in maintenance row.

text.p: WestJet Airlines Ltd, the no-frills carrier that started a series of discount fare wars in Western Canada early this year, said on Tuesday all of its flights were grounded after a maintenance dispute with Transport Canada.
WestJet said it would retain legal counsel and immediately begin a lawsuit against the government of Canada over the conflict, which is expected to keep its fleet on the tarmac for 30 days.

WestJet, in a company telephone recording, said the government agency said on September 9 that the company's maintenance program did not meet terms in an "alternate maintenance document," which was different from a previously approved manual.
The company said it volunteered at the time to change its maintenance program to comply with the alternate document, but would take some time to make the transition.

"After lengthy and detailed technical negotiations with Transport Canada, it became apparent that no such time would be granted to WestJet, even though it is customary in this industry to provide a short period of time to do so," the company said.

"This action has put WestJet Airlines in an untenable position and therefore the airline has taken the unprecedented step of cancelling flight operations until such time as this transition can be completed," it said.
Calgary-based WestJet, which started operations in February of this year, said it would immediately start processing refunds to passengers who had booked flights between now and October 17.
